Welcome to Upton Infant School
Upton Infant School
The aim of this website is to give you useful information about our school and also to reflect its ethos. Our school is welcoming and friendly with good relationships between pupils, staff, parents and carers being of paramount importance to us. We believe that children learn best when they feel safe, valued and are happy to come to school. We have high expectations of all pupils in terms of both academic achievements and behaviour. Duncan Churchill Head teacher

Curriculum

Our Aims & Values
We want all our children to love school, to see school as an exciting and happy place where they will learn interesting things, have fun and to feel successful. We want them to leave us ready for the next step in their journey so they can thrive at their next destination. Teaching children to read so they can access learning in our, and future, schools is fundamental to what we do and we are ambitious for all our children to learn to love books and to read fluently.

SEND & Inclusion
Welcome to our Inclusion Page
Information For Parents 2023
SEND Reports to Parents
The aim of the project was to find a fun way for five year olds to have the skills they need to be able to be physically fit for school that was easy to fit into a busy school day.
http://www.storycises.com/
Multi Sensory Learning
A multisensory approach is one that integrates sensory activities. The students see, hear, and touch.... In essence, a multisensory approach incorporates the learning styles for visual, auditory, kinaesthetic, and tactile learners. This would be through the use of song, manipulatives, actions and rhymes.
This is used through daily planned subjects but also planned in x 3 days a week to support more specific needs.
Differentiated teaching occurs when a teacher plans a lesson that adjusts either the content being discussed, the process used to learn or the product expected from students to ensure that learners at different starting points can receive the instruction they need to grow and succeed. Differentiation in the classroom is an important skill for teachers to give pupils the best chance at learning, regardless of their abilities, strengths and weaknesses. Pupil engagement is key to fostering motivation and confidence in the classroom.
Scaffolding refers to a method in which teachers offer a particular kind of support to pupils as they learn and develop a new concept or skill. In the scaffolding model, a teacher may share new information or demonstrate how to solve a problem. This is a temporary support which would reduce in time to encourage independence.
Metacognition is, put simply, “thinking about one's thinking.” Talking through the learning journey and modelling your thoughts to children as you go. We use the anchor chart to record this.
An anchor chart is a tool used to support instruction (i.e., “anchor” the learning for pupils). As you teach a lesson, you create a chart, together with your students, that captures the most important content and relevant strategies. This can then be sued as a prompt throughout a lesson or to reflect on prior learning.
The Graduated Response
is a way of helping to identify the needs of children and young people with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND). It provides the most effective support to help them learn and progress. This is a ‘staged’ approach and follows a four part cycle (assess, plan, do and review), known as the Graduated Response.
Plan Do Review Cycle
This cycle will involve meeting class teacher to plan a series of targets which could be met through Universal Quality First Teaching. If there is a question in regards to the barriers preventing progress it may be that either Miss Sadler or Mrs Elliott will attend the meeting and support planning around cognition and learning.
Pre-teaching is a strategy that involves teaching pupils concepts, skills, or vocabulary prior to a lesson so they can hit the ground running. It can provide pupils with more knowledge and confidence when approaching a new topic. This can help to increase engagement and reduce frustration.
Pupil Progress meetings
Individual children are discussed within a small team to ensure that we understand their needs and plan for early intervention.
Worry monster/ok not ok
All children use an emotional check in board and have access to the Worry Monster. This is used to safeguard children, regulate emotions and also form positive and trusting relationships with class teachers/Teaching assistants.
Bayley the Brilliant Dog
Bayley can come into school with the aim of providing a calming or harmonious influence that children (and perhaps sometimes the staff) can focus on to reduce classroom anxiety and stress levels. She is a Spring Spaniel aged 2 years, she loves to play ball with the children but mostly loves to hear the children read. On some occasions, whilst learning her own Brilliant Behaviour has been used to promote positive choices.
At this stage you would be invited in to discuss the concerns with Mrs Elliot, Miss Sadler and class teacher so that we can work together to support pupils. We would plan a cycle of early intervention which may include some of the targeted approaches listed below in Stage 3.
Precision Teaching is a method of planning a teaching programme to meet the needs of an individual child or young person who is experiencing difficulty with acquiring or maintaining some skills. It is one of the most effective teaching strategies for ensuring high levels of fluency and accuracy. We plan ours through ‘An Out of this World Scheme’- children are aware of their targets and see daily progress through their own record sheets.
This is a practical movement programme which meets the needs of children with motor co-ordination difficulties. We support pupils with their gross and fine motor develop, identify needs and most importantly make sure that their needs can be supported within the classroom.
Catch up Read Write Inc
This intervention teaches struggling readers to read accurately and fluently with a focus on blending at speed. It can slos be used to close the gap within sets of sounds when unknown.
ELSA- happiness club.
ELSA stands for Emotional Literacy Support Assistant. ELSA support in schools is a project designed to help schools support the emotional needs of their pupils. ELSA acknowledges that children and young people learn best when they feel happier and their emotional needs are being addressed. We jave rebranded this as ‘Happiness Club’ within our school.
NELI (Nuffield Early Language Intervention)
The Nuffield Early Language Intervention is a 20-week programme proven to help young children overcome language difficulties. It is designed for children aged 4-5 years and combines small group work with one-to-one sessions delivered by trained teaching assistants, targeting vocabulary, narrative skills, active listening and phonological awareness.
We are privileged to be able to take small groups of children to a local intervention. It has proven to:
reduce stress and anxiety, improve self-esteem, confidence and trust, encourage communication and sharing. Improve mental and physical well-being, encourage empathy and build relationships.
This intervention has a focus on number and calculation, developing children’s mathematical understanding, communication and reasoning skills. Stimulating, enjoyable games and activities engage the children and build their confidence.
Third Space at Maths
Third Space Learning is an organisation which offers online one-to-one maths tuition for primary school pupils. It is used in our school to identify and close gaps within the maths.
Despite interventions there is a specific need which falls within the following categories. A pupil at this stage would be place upon the Special Educational and Disabilities Register as they may have
Communication and Interaction
Speech, language and communication needs (SLCN) have difficulty in communicating with others, including Autism/Asperger’s.
Cognition and Learning
Support for learning difficulties may be required when children and young people learn at a slower pace than their peers, even with appropriate differentiation. children are likely to have severe and complex learning difficulties as well as a physical disability or sensory impairment. This area also includes specific learning difficulties such as dyslexia or dyscalculia.
Physical and sensory Development
Some children and young people require special educational provision because they
have a disability which prevents or hinders them from making use of the educational
facilities generally provided. This also included hearing and vision impairment.
Social and Emotional, Mental Health
Children and young people may experience a wide range of social and emotional difficulties which manifest themselves in many ways. These may include becoming withdrawn or isolated, as well as displaying challenging, disruptive or disturbing behaviour.
Speech and Language Therapists
We have strong links with the NHS Speech and Language therapists. They vist our school working alongside the children, families and staff to ensure programmes of support are in place and reviewed regularly. We also have the regular support of a highly trained Speech and Language Teaching Assistant.
Occupational Therapy/Physiotherapy
When the appropriate therapist is able to see the child, an appointment will be made to attend a clinic or the therapist will arrange to visit the school. A programme of support will be in place.
We have specialist teachers from both the Hamwic Education Trust and Dorset Council who provide support for children and staff to ensure that all pupils have the support needed to be safe and happy within school. This ranges from behaviour support, attachment to dyslexia. More Information can be found at:
https://www.dorsetnexus.org.uk/Services/817
PCPs (Pupil Centred Planning)
At Upton Infant School we have moved away for Individualised Educational Plans and have renamed them Pupil Centred Planning (PCP’s). This is a process where we work together to gain parental and child views in relation to small step targets and long term planning.
Team Around The Child (TAF)
St this stage it may be worth considering a Team Around the Child to include family members and all professionals. We would look to set outcomes which improve the progress of a child within a whole family holistic approach.
Welcome to the Hive
A snapshot of the Hive in action, filmed by pupils of Upton Infant School.
t this stage you will know us all very well and support will be well established. Below is more information about the Interventions or support which could be useful to you.

An education, health and care ( EHC ) plan is for children and young people aged up to 25 who need more support than is available through special educational needs support (stages 1-3). EHC plans identify educational, health and social needs and set out the additional support to meet those needs.
A mixed age group specialist provision within the HIVE to support complex and significant Communication and Interaction needs.
Welcome from the Honey Bees
Attention Autism is an intervention model which aims to develop natural and spontaneous communication through the use of visually based and highly motivating activities.
Introduction to Attention Autism
The PEIC-D approach revisits early interaction skills such as imitation, turn-taking and interaction. ... By working through a series of steps, using game formats, the child learns to watch others' play, join in, and then take part in turn taking sequences.
PECS is a type of Augmentative and Alternative Communication that uses visual symbols to teach the learner to communicate with parents, carers, teachers and peers. The aim is to teach intentional, functional communication and to allow users to communicate their wants and needs.
Coping In School scale
This scale is used to evaluate whether a pupil is ready to begin an integration back into a mainstream base. It is a scheme to share common criteria across and within schools for assessing and target setting for pupils with challenging behaviours.
The Skills Builder Universal Framework provides the national standard for teaching essential skills. It breaks each skill into steps, supporting progress for students of all ages and abilities - including those with special educational needs. The skills include team work, listening, communicating etc.
Is a communication system using sign based upon British Sign Language. It uses speech, sign, body, facial expressions and tone to communicate.

pageCache.pageTitle: A Brief History of Our School  | Upton Infant School
pageCache.text:
A Brief History of Our School
The original Upton Infant School was opened in January 1901, with Annie Hart as the first headteacher.
This school was based in the old church at St. Dunstans. The school had to be set up and tidied away to make way for church services. Some former pupils of the old school have shared their memories...
Just like today, the children put on a Christmas play. Here is a photograph of the Nativity play in 1946:
After fifty years, a new purpose built school was built at Guest Road. To begin with, there were just 3 classes. The first headteacher was Miss Baggs (a plaque outside the front of the school commemorates her).
In the following years the school grew and temporary classrooms were placed on the school site to accommodate the increasing number of pupils.
In 1985 a new extension was opened to house the Reception and Year One children, with the three original classrooms housing to Year Two children.
In 2000, the school celebrated the millennium by burying a time capsule out the front of the school. This is detailed in the school log books with instructions where to find it.
The school celebrated its diamond jubilee in 2012. As the current school building was opened in Queen Elizabeth II's coronation year, our jubilees mirror that of the Queen.
In 2020, like schools across the country, the school was closed to the majority of pupils due to the COVID pandemic. During this time, a reduced number of 'Key Worker' pupils attended school, with most children learning remotely with lessons delivered via the internet.
September 2022 marks the school's platinum jubilee.

The Pupil Premium is funding that school's receive to spend on children from low income families, whose parents are in the services and Looked After Children. This is to try and ensure the children achieved as well as their peers. Looked after children and children from low incomes backgrounds are, statistically, less likely to achieve. It is for the school to decide how to spend this money and we offer a number of initiatives to try and ensure that everyone who is eligible achieves well.

Rewards
All children are encouraged to do their best at Upton Infant School. Children's hard work, effort, attitude and behaviour is celebrated at our weekly Golden Assembly on Fridays.
Critterficates
Each week, every class teacher chooses two children in their class who have demonstrated outstanding behaviour, effort or attitude to learning to be rewarded with 'Critterficates'. These certificates are rewards for displaying the characteristics of learning that we teach the children through our Learning Critters. The children's names are published each fortnight in the school's Parents' Newsletter.

Governors
Welcome to our Governors’ section.
Upton Infant School is an academy that is part of a Multi Academy Trust called Hamwic Education Trust.
Information about governance at Hamwic Education Trust can be found on the Governance page of their website: https://www.hamwic.org/governance/
The Board of Trustees at Hamwic Education Trust is accountable for governance at Upton Infant School but has established a Local Governing Committee [LGC] to which it delegates specific governance functions for both Upton Infant School and Upton Junior School (known collectively as Upton Schools)

Meet the Governors
Stephen Allen
I retired a year prior to the Covid pandemic after a career transgressing logistics, as a Hazardous Goods freight manager, then data analyst for the operations team in a Boiler manufacturer company. With a will to put something back into the community I enrolled as a volunteer with both NHS and RVS. I then responded to an advertisement in the local Community magazine advising of vacancies for co-opted Governors at the school, as I am of the belief that all children should be given the best opportunities for a good education and early start in life and am pleased to be in a position to give some service in this field. Away from volunteering I am a very keen Poole Pirates Speedway follower and also a regular at Poole Town Football club matches.
Tanya Best
I have been a teacher at Upton Infant School since qualifying in 2016 and have loved teaching across all infant year groups. I currently teach in Year 2 and enjoy helping children grow in confidence and independence. Over the years, I have taken on a range of roles including leading School Council, Art and now Maths, where I support staff and pupils and contribute to developing our maths curriculum. Alongside my teaching career, I have been raising my own family, which has deepened my appreciation for the strong sense of community at Upton Infant School. I value the nurturing, family-centred ethos that supports both pupils and their families and where staff feel valued, heard and respected. I am keen to help foster and strengthen this shared sense of community across both the Infant and Junior schools as we federate. Outside of school, I enjoy spending time with my family and walking our dogs in the forest.
Alison Carter
Duncan Churchill
I have been head teacher of Upton Infant school since February 2017 and was appointed as Executive head teacher at Upton Schools, which include Upton Infant and Upton Junior schools in April 2025. I am honoured and excited to work with our school community as we develop the Federation of our two schools. Previous to working at Upton I was the head teacher of Mudeford Infant School and have previously worked at Christchurch Infant School too. Outside of work I am an avid runner who regularly runs in 5k races with my favourite distance being the marathon. I have been lucky enough to run the London marathon and the Berlin marathon twice. I am also a football fan and support Norwich City.
Diana Crisp
I am a retired teacher who worked in a local junior school for 23 years. I have also worked for Winchester University as a link tutor. This enabled me to go to many schools and help aspiring young students on their journey to be a teacher. I am also a Governor of a federated school locally which has an infant school and junior school. I was part of the governing body when it became federated and more recently became an academy. My children and grandchildren have attended Upton Infant and Upton Junior schools. Upton has been my home for 46 years and I enjoy living here very much. I hope to help to further develop the federation and look forward to working with the team of staff and Governors.
Dawn Goodwin
Rhian Homer
I am a parent governor at The Upton Schools, where my daughters currently attend. Professionally, I am a teacher and Year 6 lead at my own school, and I hope to use my experience in education to help support and develop the learning and experiences of all children at The Upton Schools. My governor role is focused largely on supporting teaching and learning across the curriculum, with a current emphasis on reading and writing. Outside of school, I enjoy music, cooking, socialising with friends and family, and relaxing with a good TV series.
Jo Shepherd
My name is Jo Shepherd and I'm the chair of the governing body at Upton Schools. I became a governor of Upton Juniors in 2021 and have been an active member of the board since then. I have held designated roles in SEND and safeguarding and was Vice Chair from 2023-2026, when I became chair. I live locally and have 3 children who have been pupils at the schools. I became a governor as I wanted to do my part in supporting the schools to flourish and provide the educational and pastoral care our children deserve.
Jill Turner
My name is Jill Turner and I am currently attempting, but failing at, a phased retirement by being a SENCO in 2 local schools. I started my journey in education as a TA in a special school, qualifying as a teacher in 2000 teaching all year groups between Nursery and Y7 in a variety of schools across BCP eventually becoming Assistant Head, DSL and SENCO in a primary school in Bournemouth. In my last 2 schools I was the staff governor and enjoy the challenges that this offers to help a school team make things even better for the children. In my spare time I play a variety of instruments including the flute and trombone. I am also learning German and Arabic on Duolingo and like to go out geocaching.
Benjamin Whittingham

Learning at home
If your child is unable to come to school, each of the year group home learning plans below has ten days of teaching for maths, literacy and another curriculum subject with activities to back up the learning objectives. They are engaging, fun and will support the in school learning. We hope you and your children enjoy doing them.
There are three 'batches' of ten day lessons for each of the year groups. Simply click on the link for batch two and so on. When your child comes back into school please bring the work in as your teachers will love to see it!

Learning Critters
We aim for children at Upton Infant School to be brilliant learners who are curious, creative, resilient and enjoy learning.
To help achieve this, children are taught to develop a range of learning skills throughout the year. The 'Learning Critters' help the children to achieve this. Find out about them below, or listen to their stories here.
